subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What trust model should OpenClaw enforce for SKILL.md skills before they enter runtime prompts and capability decisions?
rationale: The remaining work chooses security boundaries, trust roots, revocation behavior, unsigned compatibility, and possible config/profile semantics that automation should not invent.

options.title: Design the canonical trust model first
options.body: Define publisher keys, signed digests, revocation, lock/origin binding, status surfaces, and unsigned compatibility before runtime enforcement lands.

options.title: Ship advisory audit status first
options.body: Keep signatures and hashes informational for now, which reduces upgrade breakage but does not close the runtime trust boundary.

options.title: Require verified skills for full capability
options.body: Fail closed or degrade unsigned skills by default, improving security while requiring a migration and override plan for existing installations.

recommendation.title: Design the canonical trust model first
recommendation.body: Define publisher keys, signed digests, revocation, lock/origin binding, status surfaces, and unsigned compatibility before runtime enforcement lands.
